A1.justification: Both PDFs are complete, readable versions of the same theoretical work despite the changed title. Their definitions, theorems, proofs, and algorithm match reliably. Neither PDF contains an appendix.

before.justification: V1 reports mathematical definitions, constructions, and proofs, with no original experimental, simulation, or data-analysis results. Empirical studies mentioned in the introduction are attributed to other work.

after.justification: V2 remains entirely theoretical. Its added lemmas, revised proofs, and expanded literature discussion introduce no original empirical results.

M1.justification: The generation procedures in Lemmas 3.1 and 4.1 and the construction in Algorithm 1 retain their steps. The revised partition construction in Lemma 3.2 repairs a mathematical proof rather than changing the generation method.

E1.justification: Neither version uses datasets or conducts training or evaluation tasks. Newly discussed generation settings appear only as related work.

E2.justification: Neither version evaluates comparison methods or empirical baselines. The additional citations in v2 do not constitute evaluated comparators.

E3.justification: Neither version contains experimental protocols, evaluation metrics, data splits, or training settings. The theoretical generation definitions retain the same noise allowance.

E4.justification: No empirical ablations, robustness tests, sensitivity analyses, or case studies appear in either version. The adversarial language constructions remain mathematical proofs.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated runs, seeds, confidence intervals, significance tests, or statistical uncertainty estimates.

E6.justification: There are no empirical result entries in either version. The principal mathematical bounds, separations, and equivalence conclusions are retained; changes to their supporting proofs are assessed under T1.

T1.justification: V2 substantially repairs Lemma 3.2: v1 used an arbitrary partition without establishing nonempty consistency sets, whereas v2 constructs a partition satisfying that necessary condition and justifies selecting a finite witness of the required size. V2 also adds monotonicity Lemmas 2.10 and 2.13, makes the noisy-closure-dimension definition more precise, and corrects the uniform-bound argument in Lemma 4.1 and the countability wording in Lemma 4.5. These strengthen proofs supporting the central characterization results.

C1.justification: The abstract and conclusion retain the same contributions: separation between zero and one noisy string, equivalence across positive finite noise levels, and characterization of non-uniform noise-dependent generation. Theorems 2.14–2.17 in v1 correspond to 2.16–2.19 in v2 without changed claims.

C2.justification: The interpretations of the noiseless/noisy separation and the collapse across positive noise levels remain unchanged. Added proof intuition and the explicit phrase 'hierarchy collapses' explain existing conclusions without introducing new limitations or applicability claims.

D1.justification: No implementation, hyperparameter, hardware, runtime, or code/data-access information is added or revised. The additional technical material concerns mathematical reasoning rather than implementation or experimental reproducibility.

R1.justification: Section 1.1 substantially broadens its literature coverage with nine additional works, including mistake-bounded, agnostic, metric-space, replay, private, and contrastive generation and list identification. It also explicitly positions finite-noise results against the previously cited infinite-contamination work. Renamed citation keys and publication metadata updates are not counted as new works.

P1.justification: The title changes from 'Quantifying Noise in Language Generation' to 'Characterizing the Effect of Noise in Language Generation in the Limit.' V2 expands related-work prose and proof explanations and makes localized wording and notation corrections, while retaining the overall section order and narrative.

P2.justification: The displayed sequence of ordered lists in the separation proof changes from two lines to one, and the unchanged Algorithm 1 moves from midpage to a page top during reflow. The single-column design is retained, with no added figures or tables.

improvement.justification: V2 repairs an important logical gap in Lemma 3.2, which underpins the main noise-equivalence and characterization results. V1 inferred a dimension bound from finite closure without ensuring the required nonempty consistency sets; v2 explicitly constructs a partition ensuring them. Together with the supporting monotonicity proofs and corrected quantifier arguments, this substantially improves mathematical reliability while preserving the headline conclusions.
